bites.title: Rhythm before beauty
bites.body: Hatching is rhythm. Here I'm counting marks, not judging each one, so go fast and don't fuss. Quantity first. Quality shows up on its own.

bites.title: Fill the lanes
bites.body: Ten lanes: start each mark on a red dot, flick it into the ring. One mark per lane.

bites.title: Metronome
bites.body: Twenty marks in 15 seconds, anywhere in the lanes. Tick, tick, tick. Let the shoulder do it.

bites.title: Parallel
bites.body: Ten more, and this time keep them parallel. Lock the wrist, slide the whole arm.

bites.title: Crosshatch
bites.body: New lanes at the opposite angle, right over your first set. Ten marks. Crosshatching is just two rhythms stacked.

bites.title: Ghosting: five confident lines
bites.body:
Pick two points. Hover above the canvas and rehearse the motion three times without touching. Then put it down in one smooth pass.

Five of those in a row, each fast and straight.
bites.hint: The rehearsal is the trick. Your arm learns the path before the pen commits.
bites.praise: Five for five. That's a trained arm.

bites.title: 06 cleared
bites.body: Lanes, metronome, parallel, crosshatch, ghosting. The Dojo's Rhythm drill counts clean marks in 10 seconds. Beat your best every morning.
